old_digest: Neither a “No-ball” nor a “Wide ball” shall be reckoned as one of the “Over.”
new_digest: Neither a “no-ball” nor a “wide-ball” shall be reckoned as one of the “over.”

old_digest: From a “wide ball” as many runs as are run shall be added to the score as “wide balls,” and if no run be otherwise obtained one run shall be so added.
new_digest: From a “wide-ball” as many runs as are run shall be added to the score as “wide balls,” and if no runs be otherwise obtained one run shall be so added.

old_digest: At the beginning of the match, and of each innings, the umpire at the bowler’s wicket shall call “Play”; from that time no trial ball shall be allowed to any bowler on the ground between the wickets, and when one of the batsmen is out the use of the bat shall not be allowed to any person until the next batsman shall come in.
new_digest: At the beginning of the match, and of each innings, the umpire at the bowler’s wicket shall call “Play” from that time. No trial ball shall be allowed to any bowler on the ground between the wickets, and when one of the batsmen is out the use of the bat shall not be allowed to any person until the next batsman shall come in.

old_digest: A run is scored—1st, So often as the batsmen after a hit, or at any time while the ball is in play, shall have crossed, and made good their ground from end to end.
new_digest: 1st So often as the batsmen after a hit, or at any time while the ball is in play, shall have crossed, and made good their ground from end to end;

old_digest: It shall measure not less than 9in. nor more than 9¼in. in circumference.
new_digest: It shall measure not less than 9in. nor more than 9½in. in circumference.

old_digest: If the umpire at the bowler’s end be not satisfied of the absolute fairness of the delivery of any ball, he shall call “No ball.” 48*. The umpire shall take especial care to call “No-ball” instantly upon delivery, “Wide ball” as soon as it shall have passed the striker.
new_digest: If the umpire at the bowler’s end be not satisfied of the absolute fairness of the delivery of any ball, he shall call “No ball.” 48½. The umpire shall take especial care to call “No ball” instantly upon delivery, “Wide ball” as soon as it shall have passed the striker.

old_digest: The bat shall not exceed 4½ in. in the widest part; it shall not be more than 38in. in length.
new_digest: The bat shall not exceed 4¼in. in the widest part; it shall not be more than 38in. in length.

old_digest: The side which goes in second shall follow their innings, if they have scored eighty runs less than the opposite side.
new_digest: The side which goes in second shall follow their innings, if they have scored 120 runs less than the opposite side in a threedays match, or 80 runs in a two-days match.

old_digest: The bails shall be each 4⅝in. in length, and when in position, on the top of the stumps, shall not project more than ¾in. above them. The wickets shall not be changed during a match, unless the ground between them become unfit for play, and then only by consent of both sides.
new_digest: The bails shall be each 4¼in. in length, and when in position, on the top of the stumps, shall not project more than ¾in. above them. The wickets shall not be changed during the match, unless the ground between them becomes unfit for play, and then only by consent of both sides.
